title: Same Verdict, Different Reasons: LLM-as-a-Judge and Clinician Disagreement on Medical Chatbot Completeness

paper.authors: DeLucia, Huang, Joshi, Yarmohammadi, Hassoon, Dredze (Johns Hopkins Data Science and AI Institute)
paper.repo_absent_reason: The paper releases no code and no data: a full-text search for github / repository / 'code available' / anonymous-supplement links returns nothing, and the only external links are the two Hugging Face model cards (meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, aaditya/OpenBioLLM-Llama3-70B). Prompts are printed verbatim in Appendix D (Tables 4-10).
paper.tierb_relation: NO UPGRADE. A Tier B prompt-level config already exists (harness/tierb/configs/W7155245470.json, status needs_human) and remains the best available protocol, because there is no repository to upgrade to. This card adds what Tier B left open: the ground-truth construction pass, the subset-filter reconstruction and the cost of both.
paper.third_party_code: The grading machinery the paper builds on IS public: openai/simple-evals (MIT, commit 652c89d0ca9df547706735883097e9537d40dc47, shallow clone at external/repos/W4400222256/openai__simple-evals). healthbench_eval.py carries the oss_eval data URL and a GRADER_TEMPLATE that matches the paper's Table 4 boolean grader almost word for word, so the clinician-ground-truth pass can be run with released code.

dependence.note: The subject of the study is the LLM judge itself: every number in Table 1 is a property of gpt-5-mini's grading decisions. The comparison label ('clinician ground truth') is, on HealthBench, itself produced by an LLM - a GPT-4.1 pass over the clinician-written positive rubric criteria - so a re-execution carries model dependence on BOTH sides and both must be re-run.

claim.statement: On the 1,281 filtered single-turn layperson HealthBench conversations, gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 used as a judge with the zero-shot Analytical-Rubric (5-point completeness, threshold score >= 4 = complete) reaches the study's ceiling for detecting incomplete responses and still discriminates barely above chance: F1 = 0.76, precision = 0.86, recall = 0.68, AUC = 0.66 against the clinician ground truth (Table 1, HealthBench block, row Analytical-Rubric, GPT-5 Mini columns; Sec. 4.1).
claim.metric: F1 of the Incomplete class (judge score < 4 vs ground-truth incomplete) plus precision, recall and AUC of the raw 1-5 judge score, over the 1,281 conversations. Ground truth: the HealthBench 'ideal' answer is graded criterion-by-criterion by GPT-4.1 against the conversation's positive completeness rubric items (equal weights, binary met/not-met); complete iff >= 75% of criteria are satisfied (77% of the 1,281 come out incomplete).
claim.original_source: Table 1 (p. 6, HealthBench block); Sec. 4.1 'GPT-5 Mini with Analytical-Rubric sets the performance ceiling'; Sec. 3.2 for the 1,281-conversation filter and the 75% ground-truth threshold; App. B.2 for the filtering pipeline.

protocol.model_usage_verified: yes - Sec. 3.1: 'three backbone LLM Judges: Llama 3.3-70B, OpenBioLLM-70B, and GPT-5 Mini (gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07)'; 'GPT-5 Mini was run at the default temperature of 1.0'. No alias inference needed. The gpt-4-turbo hit in live_ids is a citation of prior work in Sec. 2, not an experimental arm.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (App. C: 'GPT-5-Mini was accessed via OpenAI API')
protocol.prompt_source: Paper App. D, Table 9 'Full grading prompt for the Analytical-Rubric rubric' (transcribed verbatim into harness/tierb/configs/W7155245470.json, field prompt.user_template). Table 10 holds the FSS variant, Tables 7-8 General-Likert, Tables 4-6 Dynamic-Checklist. Ground-truth grader prompt: Table 4 = the openai/simple-evals healthbench GRADER_TEMPLATE.

params.response_format: structured JSON output ('Return a valid JSON object with the following fields: "explanation" and "criteria_score"')
params.reasoning_effort: not stated by the paper (API default assumed)
params.params_source: Sec. 3.1 ('a maximum of 4,096 output tokens and structured JSON output'; 'GPT-5 Mini was run at the default temperature of 1.0'); App. C

protocol.seeds_note: Temperature 1.0 on a reasoning model makes a single pass a draw from a wide distribution; the paper reports one pass. 3 seeds, median, with the run-to-run spread reported as a new number.
protocol.input_construction: The conversation is flattened to a single string with 'User:' / 'Assistant:' role prefixes (App. B.2) and the HealthBench ideal_completion is appended as the last assistant turn - the judged response is the ideal answer, not a model answer.
protocol.output_parse: read criteria_score (integer 1-5) from the returned JSON after stripping any markdown fence; score >= 4 -> complete, else incomplete; unparsable replies retried once and then counted as incomplete and reported.
protocol.ground_truth_pass: Separate one-shot pass with gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 (paper says 'GPT-4.1', undated): for each of the 1,281 conversations, one call per POSITIVE completeness-axis rubric criterion, boolean met/not-met (Table 4 grader), equal weights; complete iff the satisfied fraction >= 0.75.
protocol.evaluation: Binary F1/precision/recall of the Incomplete class plus ROC-AUC on the raw 1-5 score, over the 1,281 items (plain scikit-learn; no released script).

artifacts.prompts_path: paper App. D Tables 4-10 (no repository); transcribed in harness/tierb/configs/W7155245470.json
artifacts.data_path: HealthBench oss_eval split, https://openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/simple-evals/healthbench/2025-05-07-06-14-12_oss_eval.jsonl (60 MB, 5,000 conversations; fields prompt, rubrics[criterion/points/tags], example_tags, ideal_completions_data, prompt_id) - the 1,281-conversation filtered subset is NOT released. MedExpert (108 questions x 5 responses) comes from a separate ML4H 2025 paper by the same group; its availability is not stated here.
artifacts.eval_path: none released. The ground-truth grader is reproducible from openai/simple-evals healthbench_eval.py (GRADER_TEMPLATE, _compute_clipped_score); the F1/AUC computation is trivial and must be re-implemented.
artifacts.data_public: partial - HealthBench yes, the 1,281-item filter and the derived clinician ground truth no, MedExpert unknown
artifacts.redistributable: yes for HealthBench-derived artifacts under MIT with attribution; our reconstructed filter list and ground-truth labels are new artifacts we can publish alongside the run
artifacts.notes: No PHI or PII: HealthBench conversations are synthetic and MedExpert is clinician-curated (paper App. B.1). Because both the item set and the labels have to be rebuilt, our n will not be exactly 1,281 and our ground truth will not be bit-identical to theirs - both must be reported as reconstruction deltas.

blockers: The 1,281-conversation subset is not released. Reproducing it needs the App. B.2 cascade: langid language filter, heuristic HCP tags (799 flagged), then a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct few-shot classifier with the vocabulary constrained to True/False (828 more flagged, Table 3 prompt). Metadata-only filters give a different, larger set, so the item count will differ either way.

The clinician ground truth is not released and is itself an LLM product: it requires a full GPT-4.1 grading pass (~12.8k calls, ~$46) before the subject model can be scored, and the paper does not give the GPT-4.1 snapshot date, so label noise is added on top of subject-model drift.
Judge decoding is temperature 1.0 with an unstated reasoning effort, so both passes are stochastic; the published Table 1 is a single draw.
MedExpert (the second dataset, best AUC 0.56) is from a separate paper with no stated availability - the MedExpert half of Table 1 is out of scope for this card.

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (P0); the paper's best judge and the source of the headline ceiling

successors: gpt-5.6-terra (vendor-designated replacement for gpt-5-mini per the OpenAI deprecations page)
auxiliary_models_not_under_test: gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 - ground-truth grader only (its snapshot is alive; it is not the object of the claim)
meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct - HCP filter classifier (open weights, hash-pinned)
arms.open_weight_anchor: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and OpenBioLLM-Llama3-70B are the paper's other two judges and give a permanent re-execution axis (both hash-pinnable, greedy decoding).

budget.assumptions: Subject pass: 1,281 items x 3 seeds = 3,843 calls, ~1,600 input tokens (the ~700-token Analytical-Rubric prompt plus the conversation and the ideal answer) and ~900 output tokens (reasoning plus the JSON explanation) -> $1.5 in + $6.9 out = ~$8.5. Ground-truth pass (run once, not per seed): ~10 positive completeness criteria per conversation x 1,281 = ~12,810 calls at ~1,200 in / ~150 out with gpt-4.1 -> ~$46. Total ~$55; the ground-truth pass is 84% of it and is reusable across every seed, rubric variant and successor arm.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Primary number: F1 of the Incomplete class for gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 with the zero-shot Analytical-Rubric (median of 3 seeds) against 0.76, with AUC 0.66 as the claim-bearing secondary. Survival = F1 inside the bootstrap 95% CI over items around 0.76 AND the paper's actual argument holds: AUC stays in the near-chance band (<= ~0.70), so the judge still offers no triage utility. Partial = F1 moves outside the CI but AUC remains near chance, or vice versa. Death = AUC rises to a genuinely discriminative level (>= ~0.80) on a comparably reconstructed ground truth, which would overturn the paper's central 'LLM judges cannot separate complete from incomplete' conclusion. Because prevalence is 77% incomplete, F1 alone is weak evidence and must always be read next to AUC and next to the majority-class baseline.
judgment.notes: The reconstruction deltas (our n vs 1,281; our incomplete prevalence vs 0.77) are reported first, and the judgment is conditioned on them. A same-ground-truth ablation (our GPT-4.1 labels vs a second GPT-4.1 pass) bounds label noise before any model-drift conclusion is drawn.

user_checks: Ground truth: spend ~$46 on the GPT-4.1 grading pass to rebuild the labels (required for any comparison to Table 1), or drop this card?
Subset: reproduce the App. B.2 filter including the local Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct HCP classifier, or approximate with metadata-only filters and report the item-count delta?
Which GPT-4.1 snapshot for the ground truth - gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 (the only dated one) - and do we accept that the paper only wrote 'GPT-4.1'?
Scope: HealthBench Analytical-Rubric only, or also the FSS variant (0.83/0.62) so the 'few-shot shifts threshold, not discrimination' claim can be judged for ~$8 more?
domain_notes: The judged text is always HealthBench's own clinician-written 'ideal' answer, so the task is: does a judge agree with clinicians about what is missing from a response that clinicians consider good? 77% of these ideal answers fail the 75%-of-criteria bar, which is why F1 for the Incomplete class can be high (0.76) while AUC is barely above chance (0.66). The Dynamic-Checklist row on HealthBench (F1 0.93, AUC 0.93) is excluded by the authors as circular - its judge and the ground truth share the same ICL rubric scoring - and must stay excluded in any re-run. The paper's deeper finding (RQ3: agreeing verdicts cite different omissions) rests on a GPT-5 Mini failure-mode classifier over different-verdict pairs and is a separate, larger card.
